THE COMPANY
Established in early 2024, at Analogue Insight we are bridging the Analogue and Digital Worlds for Tomorrow through our Chiplet Solutions. Our core expertise lies in developing cutting-edge Chiplet technology that serves as the building block for advanced communication systems. Our Chiplets are designed to offer high performance, scalability, and integration flexibility, enabling our clients to achieve breakthroughs in computation speed, data processing, and connectivity. For more information about us, check out our website (Analogue Insight) and LinkedIn Page (Analogue Insight™: Overview | LinkedIn).

THE ROLE
We are seeking an exceptional Chief Technology Officer (High-Speed Analog) to lead the technical vision of Analogue Insight as we grow from a fast-moving start-up into a scale-up. As CTO, you will own the technology strategy for our electrical and photonic interconnect portfolio – 112G/224G-class SerDes, 32G/64G UCIe die-to-die PHYs, high-bandwidth memory interfaces, data converters (ADC/DAC) and optical I/O – and drive it across our customer programmes and product roadmap. You will lead the CTO Office, act as the company's senior technical voice with customers, partners, foundries and investors, and build deep links between Analogue Insight and leading universities and research institutes.
This role is ideal for a recognised leader in high-speed analog and mixed-signal design, with strong academic standing and strong ties to industry. We particularly welcome candidates with a professorship or senior research background who want to see their work reach customer silicon.
Location: Fully remote, ideally based in the UK, Europe, Armenia, India, Canada or the US.
Reporting to: CEO, as a member of the executive team.
Hiring Manager: Christian Borelli, Founder, CEO & CPO.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Technology Vision & Strategy: Define and own Analogue Insight's long-term technology vision for electrical and photonic interconnect, grounded in first-principles engineering and aligned with market needs, customer roadmaps and the company's growth plans.
  • IP & Product Roadmap: Translate the strategy into a clear multi-year IP roadmap – next-generation SerDes, UCIe die-to-die links, high-bandwidth memory interfaces, data converters and optical I/O – prioritising investment, tape-outs and advanced-node choices, and owning technical risk mitigation, with the CEO and executive team.
  • Architecture & Technical Authority: Act as the final technical authority on architecture, circuit approaches and design methodology, setting aggressive performance, power, area and robustness targets, and leading technical reviews across architecture, analog/mixed-signal, digital, layout and validation.
  • Hardest Technical Problems: Personally drive resolution of the most challenging circuit and system issues through first-principles analysis, modelling, simulation and silicon-based investigation.
  • Design Closure & Silicon Success: Ensure robust design closure – post-layout verification, performance optimisation and silicon-to-model correlation – so that our IP is first-time-right in customer silicon.
  • CTO Office & Technical Leadership: Build and lead the CTO Office and the technical leadership team, mentoring senior and principal engineers, raising the technical bar and shaping our technical career track.
  • Research & Innovation: Lead advanced R&D and technology exploration, driving architectural innovation in high-speed analog, mixed-signal and photonic circuits, and growing a strong patent and publication portfolio.
  • Academic & Research Partnerships: Leverage your network to build and lead partnerships with top universities and research institutes, including joint research programmes, funded projects, PhD and post-doc collaborations, and talent pipelines.
  • Customer & Industry Engagement: Serve as the senior technical voice of the company with customers, foundries, EDA vendors, standards bodies and ecosystem partners, supporting key wins and strategic engagements.
  • Investor & Board Support: Represent the technology vision to investors, advisors and the board, and support technical due diligence for fundraising, grants and potential acquisitions.
  • Engineering Excellence: Promote rigorous engineering practices, design quality and knowledge sharing, and champion design automation, simulation automation and AI-assisted design to scale productivity and quality.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR
Must-have Technical skills:
  • Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering or a related field, with a focus on high-speed analog/mixed-signal circuit design
  • 15+ years of combined industry and/or academic experience in high-speed analog design, including senior technical leadership roles
  • World-class expertise in at least one of: high-speed wireline transceivers (SerDes, die-to-die links), clocking and PLLs, or high-speed data converters – with a strong system-level view across the full link
  • Strong understanding of advanced CMOS (FinFET and beyond), packaging and chiplet integration, and the interaction between circuits, channels and systems
  • Proven track record of taking complex designs from architecture to successful silicon
  • Strong academic and industry standing, evidenced by publications at leading venues (e.g. ISSCC, VLSI, JSSC, CICC), patents and invited talks
  • An established network across leading universities, research institutes and the semiconductor industry
  • Experience building and leading high-performing technical teams, ideally including distributed or remote teams
Nice-to-have:
  • Current or past professorship or senior research position at a leading university
  • Deep, hands-on expertise in one or more of the following circuit areas:
    • Fractional-N PLLs, LC-VCOs, DTC/TDC, multi-modulus dividers
    • Phase interpolators, injection-locked oscillators, multi-phase clock generation
    • High-speed time-interleaved DACs and line drivers
    • TIAs, CTLEs, PGAs and other high-bandwidth amplifiers
    • Time-interleaved SAR ADCs and track-and-hold circuits
    • Bandgaps, LDOs, temperature sensors and other precision/support circuits
  • Experience in photonic or optical interconnect (e.g. TIAs, drivers, co-packaged optics)
  • Experience with circuit modelling, simulation automation, optimisation and silicon-to-model correlation
  • Involvement in standards bodies or consortia (e.g. UCIe, JEDEC, OIF, IEEE)
  • Experience securing and leading funded research programmes and industry–academia collaborations
  • Start-up or scale-up experience, including working with investors and boards

Soft & Professional Skills:
  • Inspiring, clear communication in professional English – able to engage engineers, customers, academics and investors alike
  • Strategic thinker who is also comfortable going deep into technical details
  • Collaborative, feedback-oriented leadership style that builds trust across a remote team
  • Demonstrated ability to mentor and grow senior engineers and future technical leaders
  • Strong ownership, reliability, and follow-through
  • High level of integrity and professionalism in representing the company and handling sensitive information
  • We are looking for a technical leader who combines deep circuit-design expertise with architectural thinking, research vision and hands-on execution to solve the hardest problems in next-generation high-speed connectivity – and who can build a team that does the same.

OUR CULTURE
We’re a fully remote team of around 25 people distributed across the UK, Armenia, Italy, the US, Estonia, India, and beyond. We believe great talent is everywhere!
  • Our values are our north star:We Grow Together, We Win Together. Excellence Builds Relationships. Trust Is Our Currency. Results Matter, but People Create Them.
  • Connected, even remotely:We invest intentionally in staying connected through regular all-hands, 1:1s, technical reviews, and informal coffee chats, so collaboration feels natural and human despite the distance.
  • High ownership, real impact:Everyone contributes directly to customer-facing IP. Your work doesn’t disappear into layers of management – it ships.
  • How we work:We move fast but thoughtfully, communicate openly, and balance autonomy with support. Technical decisions are debated openly and grounded in data, trade-offs, and first-principles thinking.

WHY JOIN US
  • Remote-first flexibility – work from anywhere, with flexible hours
  • Equipment & setup – we’ll provide the tools you need to succeed
  • High-impact projects – design real analog IP used in customer silicon
  • Supportive team culture – a dedicated manager and a team of colleagues ready to help
  • Competitive, transparent compensation– adjusted for your location and engagement model
  • Learning & growth – AI–DLP sessions, technical deep dives, and peer-led knowledge sharing that build both technical depth and system-level perspective

RECRUITMENT PROCESS
  1. Founder Call (30 min) – mutual introduction and interest alignment
  2. Technical Interview(90 min) – fundamentals, reasoning, and problem-solving
  3. Second Technical Interview (60 min) – another deep-dive into specific topics, which might include a presentation that we'll let you know about in advance
  4. Senior Management Discussion (60 min) – another deep-dive into specific topics with our Senior Management Team
  5. HR & Culture Call (45 min)–values, collaboration style, and ways of working
  6. Offer & Next Steps– we send the offer and kick off the onboarding process.
Disclaimer: This is our standard process for most roles. For more senior, specialized, or higher-authority positions, we reserve the right to amend or tailor these steps as we see fit.

If you don’t meet every requirement but feel excited about the role, apply anyway. We value curiosity, integrity, and potential as much as experience.

jobs.description:
This is a remote position.

Meta Description:Join Rutherford’s Talent Clearinghouse as an executive mentor, coach or specialist consultant supporting employee development through the Talent Accelerator.

Executive Mentors, Coaches & Specialist Consultants
Evergreen Expression of Interest — Rutherford Talent Clearinghouse™
Executive Talent Accelerator Programme
Canada · United States · United Kingdom

Put your experience to work developing others

Rutherford International welcomes expressions of interest from experienced executives, professional coaches and subject-matter specialists who can help professionals strengthen their performance, develop their judgement and prepare for greater responsibility.

Through the Executive Talent Accelerator, Rutherford matches assessed employees of enterprise clients with development expertise suited to their objectives, behavioural profiles and organisational circumstances.

This posting recruits independent providers of mentoring, coaching and specialist consulting services. It is an Evergreen Expression of Interest, not a current vacancy or a guaranteed assignment.

Augmenting internal career development

The Executive Talent Accelerator augments employers’ internal career and leadership development programmes with dedicated mentoring capacity, structured coaching and targeted specialist expertise.

Annual reviews can establish clear development priorities, but managers’ operational responsibilities may leave limited time for consistent guidance, practice and follow-up. Effective mentoring and coaching also require capabilities and interpersonal qualities that differ from those needed to manage performance.

Rutherford provides additional support to help employees act on agreed development objectives, working alongside their employer’s internal programme.

Three distinct ways to contribute

Executive Mentors

Provide longer-term, holistic guidance grounded in personal experience, career wisdom and relevant leadership responsibilities. Mentors help participants examine career direction, navigate organisational challenges, strengthen judgement and prepare for broader responsibilities.

Effective mentors explain their reasoning, share relevant experience and help participants develop their own judgement.

Executive Coaches

Provide structured, focused support for short-term skill development and performance improvement. Coaches help participants establish specific objectives, practise new approaches and review progress against agreed outcomes.

Assignments may address communication, delegation, stakeholder relationships, leadership behaviours or readiness for a defined responsibility.

Subject-Matter Specialist Consultants

Provide focused expertise addressing a particular functional, technical or business need. Specialists may explain a method, examine a decision, review work or help participants apply unfamiliar knowledge.

The scope, intended contribution and limits of the advice are established for each assignment. Implementation work is agreed separately.

Professionals may offer more than one service. Suitability and engagement scope are considered separately for each role.

Who should register

We welcome:

  • Current and former executives with relevant leadership experience and a demonstrated ability to develop others.
  • Professional coaches who can explain their methods, qualifications and evidence of contribution.
  • Senior functional and technical specialists who can translate expertise into practical learning.
  • Experienced consultants interested in supporting enterprise-sponsored development.

A distinguished career or senior title alone does not establish mentoring or coaching capability. We look for evidence that you can listen, explain, challenge appropriately and adapt your approach to another person’s needs.

Assessment and matching

Rutherford evaluates providers across three complementary areas:

  • Functional expertise:demonstrated knowledge, judgement and relevant experience.
  • Development capability:the ability to mentor, coach or teach effectively within the service offered.
  • Service orientation and relationship fit:the motivation and interpersonal capacity to support another person’s progress.

The RutherfordINTEL Assessment informs curator review alongside professional history, qualifications, references and examples of developmental work.

Matching considers the employee’s objectives, behavioural profile, enterprise context and practical needs, together with the provider’s expertise, approach and availability.

Working with Rutherford and enterprise clients

Rutherford International markets the Executive Talent Accelerator, holds and manages the enterprise client relationship, coordinates development mandates and matches providers to participating employees.

Providers deliver agreed services as independent contractors to Rutherford International. Each assignment establishes the scope, objectives, professional fees, time commitment, reporting requirements and engagement terms.

Providers are expected to:

  • Prepare thoroughly and deliver relevant, actionable guidance.
  • Maintain accurate timesheets and submit them through the agreed process.
  • Support development objectives aligned with the client’s internal programme.
  • Respect confidentiality and agreed information-sharing boundaries.
  • Disclose conflicts and work within their professional competence.
  • Distinguish developmental support from management authority or separately commissioned implementation work.
  • Review progress and raise concerns when the match or scope needs to change.

Employer sponsorship does not automatically provide access to private assessment results or confidential development discussions.

Assessment, membership and assignment fees

Initial expression of interest — Free

Registering creates no payment obligation.

Assessment and feedback — USD $250

If invited to proceed, this stage includes behavioural and leadership profiling, relevant benchmark interpretation and professional feedback.

Clearinghouse directory membership — USD $125 per month, with a 12-month term

For accepted members, membership includes assistance with the Rutherford Consultant Thesis™, business-development profiling, talent promotion, lead generation, sector research community access and career or project-success advisory support.

Rutherford-managed Accelerator assignments

Rutherford invoices the enterprise client for agreed services delivered by the provider.

Rutherford retains20% of professional billings, excluding applicable taxes. The provider receives the remaining80% of professional billings, subject to the agreed engagement terms.

This service fee isadditional to the monthly directory membership feeand reflects Rutherford’s client acquisition, matching, programme coordination, client relationship management and billing responsibilities.

Membership does not guarantee assignments or income.

Conversion to employment

If a consulting assignment converts to employment with the contracting client, the client pays a conversion fee of25% of annual salary and bonus income before six months from the assignment’s start, or20% from six months to one year.

Rutherford International retains agency rights for12 months after the consulting assignment ends.

Register your interest

Select“I’m interested”to complete Rutherford International’s Talent Registration form.

Indicate whether you wish to be considered as an executive mentor, executive coach, subject-matter specialist consultant or a combination of these roles.

Following initial review, a curator may invite you to provide further information and proceed to assessment and membership consideration.

Registration does not guarantee acceptance, representation, a client introduction or an assignment.

jobs.description:
Rapid7's vulnerability intelligence team does industry-leading offensive research that helps organizations worldwide understand and prioritize real risk. When a critical vulnerability starts getting exploited in the wild, we're the team that figures out what's actually happening, how bad it is, and what defenders need to do about it. We're looking for an experienced vulnerability researcher to help lead that work, with a strong focus on rapid n-day analysis and on making Metasploit better for the security community.


About the Team

Rapid7 vulnerability researchers analyze high-priority n-day vulnerabilities, write Metasploit modules, find and publish zero-day vulnerabilities, and help customers, the media, internal teams, and the public understand which threats matter and why. We drive Rapid7's company-wide Emergent Threat Response (ETR) program, coordinating our research, product coverage, and customer guidance when widespread attacks hit. We aren't satisfied with being purely reactive, though. We also look for the vulnerabilities and attack patterns that will become tomorrow's widespread threats.


About the Role

This role sits at the Staff level, a senior technical leadership position on our individual contributor track. Your time will be focused primarily on Emergent Threat Response and Metasploit, with zero-day research as a secondary focus.


Primary focus: Emergent Threat Response (n-day research)

  • Rapidly analyze newly disclosed and actively exploited vulnerabilities, often under tight timelines, to determine root cause, exploitability, and real-world impact
  • Reproduce vulnerabilities and build working exploits from patch diffs, advisories, and limited public information, documenting behavioral differences across affected versions and platforms
  • Publish clear, technically rigorous root cause analyses that help defenders act quickly and reflect Rapid7's attacker-focused approach to vulnerability intelligence
  • Advise detection and vulnerability check engineers as they build coverage, and help internal teams and customers understand what's urgent, what isn't, and why
  • Serve as a go-to expert during high-velocity events (think Log4Shell), knowing when to raise alarms and when to counsel patience

Primary focus: Metasploit

  • Develop and contribute high-quality exploit modules to Metasploit, especially for high-priority vulnerabilities coming out of ETR work
  • Drive improvements to the Metasploit Framework itself, including new capabilities, tooling, library enhancements, and quality improvements that make the framework more effective for researchers and practitioners
  • Review community and internal module contributions, raising the bar for code qua
  • lity, reliability, and stability across the project
  • Partner with the Metasploit engineering team on roadmap priorities and help shape where the framework goes next

Secondary focus: Zero-day research

  • Identify and research, new vulnerabilities in technologies that matter to enterprise organizations
  • Help define longer-term research priorities with the broader team, bringing a point of view on emerging attack surface

Across all of it

  • Contribute technical trend analysis to Rapid7's research reports and publications
  • Represent the team's work through conference talks, webcasts, blog posts, and media engagements
  • Mentor and develop other researchers through code review, pairing, documentation, and technical guidance
  • Explain technical risk clearly to audiences ranging from engineers to executives

The skills and qualities you'll bring include

  • Demonstrable expertise across most major vulnerability classes and exploitation techniques, with the ability to reproduce vulnerabilities and attacks quickly and effectively
  • Experience developing complex exploit chains from scratch, including from patch diffs or minimal public detail
  • Strong reverse engineering and binary/code diffing skills, including against large codebases or binaries
  • Expert-level understanding of networking, operating system internals for one or more major OSes, and/or bypassing common exploit mitigations
  • A track record of writing about vulnerabilities and exploits for a public audience, and of speaking about your research at conferences, on webcasts, or similar venues
  • The ability to build custom tooling as needed and to scope work into clear milestones rather than monolithic deliverables
  • A willingness to mentor and teach. You don't need to be a people manager, but you should enjoy making the people around you better.
  • Communicate in a clear manner that conveys objectives and rationale when explaining complex attack patterns and risks to technical stakeholders and detection engineers.
  • Eager and open to understanding "why" a change is happening, acting as an active driver of it, and focusing forward versus in the past to tackle emerging threats.

MonetizeMore is a global leader in ad tech, trusted by thousands of web publishers and app developers across the globe.   1. Champion Product Excellence: You will mentor and guide other Product Managers across MonetizeMore, transforming our product organization into a best-in-class, outcome-driven Product Operating Model (inspired by modern frameworks like Marty Cagan’s Silicon Valley Product Group).
  2. Own the Product Management for Advanced Ads (Interim): You will drive the strategy, growth, and execution of Advanced Ads—our leading ad-management platform powering over 150,000 websites worldwide.

You don't just build features to check boxes; you build solutions that move the needle on business goals, and you enable the PMs on your team to do the same.

Core Responsibilities

1. Leadership & Product Operating Model Excellence

  • Mentorship & Coaching: Serve as a player-coach to other Product Managers, guiding them to elevate their product craft, execution, and strategic thinking.
  • Outcome over Output: Evangelize the shift from feature-factory mindsets to an outcome-driven culture. Train PMs to obsess over business results and customer impact rather than sprint velocity and story points.
  • Framework Standardizing: Implement modern product operating model principles (e.g., product trios, data-informed decision making, rapid prototyping, and de-risking assumptions).
  • Evangelize Kaizen: Introduce continuous feedback loops and structured retrospective frameworks to scale product management maturity across the entire organization.

2. Product Ownership: Advanced Ads

  • Strategy & Vision: Define and execute the long-term product vision for Advanced Ads, integrating its flexible ad injection, targeting, and Google Ad Manager capabilities deeper into the MonetizeMore ecosystem.
  • Continuous Discovery: Lead continuous product discovery to uncover publishers' deepest pain points, validating ideas for usability, feasibility, viability, and value before writing code.
  • Revenue & Growth: Take end-to-end ownership from monetization strategy to GTM. Prioritize the roadmap based on clear ROI, keeping a laser focus on customer lifetime value (LTV) and monthly recurring revenue (MRR).
  • Cross-Functional Alignment: Collaborate with Engineering, Design, and Growth to ensure features aren't just shipped, but successfully adopted and commercialized.
  • Long-Term Plan: Determine the long term needs of this business line: resource requirements, investment, propose and collaborate on the best organizational design for the success of the product.
Who You Are
  • The Experienced Leader: You have 8+ years of Product Management experience, with at least 3+ years leading or mentoring other PMs. Ad tech, SaaS, or WordPress ecosystem experience is a massive plus.
  • The Operating Model Expert: You have deeply practical experience working within a modern, empowerment-based Product Operating Model. You know what "good" looks like and possess the empathy and patience to coach others there.
  • The Owner Mindset: You treat your product like your own business. You aren't afraid to dive into raw data to find hidden patterns or jump on a customer call to understand friction points.
  • Data-Driven & Courageous: You monitor product health metrics religiously. If the data shows a feature is failing to deliver the expected outcome, you have the courage to pivot or kill it.
  • The Clear Communicator: You effortlessly translate complex technical logic or abstract product frameworks into digestible, high-impact value propositions for stakeholders, engineers, and your team.

What We Offer

  • True Flexibility: Work from anywhere in the world with a flexible schedule that fits your lifestyle.

jobs.description:
Who we are

For more than 40 years, Reworld has been a leader in sustainable waste solutions, providing our customers with innovative solutions that help them achieve carbon-negative outcomes.

Our Vision

Reworld is leading the charge to a carbon-negative future through revolutionary sustainable materials management solutions that reduce, reuse, recycle and reimagine waste for the benefit of society and the environment.

Our Business

Reworld partners with businesses by offering cutting-edge engineering and innovative solutions, to help customers reduce, reuse, recycle and recover value from waste streams and meet or exceed their sustainability goals.

Our Value

Reworld's differentiator comes from our ecosystem of technology, facilities and partnerships, trusted by the world’s largest organizations to reimagine waste management for a smarter, more sustainable world.

All that we’re missing is you. Apply today!

About the role

Scope of Role:

The Director of Electrical Engineering leads the Electrical Design Engineering team and is accountable for all electrical design activities supporting the Energy-from-Waste process across more than 30 facilities across North America. This role provides design leadership for electrical infrastructure across high-voltage (26 kV to 230 kV), medium-voltage (5 kV to 13.8 kV), and low-voltage systems, including high-voltage breakers, step-up transformers, turbine generators, balance-of-plant equipment, medium-voltage switchgear, motor control centers (MCCs), fans and motors, protective relaying, and short-circuit and arc-flash studies.

The Electrical Design Engineering team also supports a broad range of plant systems and disciplines, including steam generation boilers and auxiliaries, feedwater pumps, deaerator systems, turbine generators, condensers, air pollution control equipment, ash handling and conveying equipment, and metals recovery systems. This position leads a team of electrical subject matter experts (SMEs) supporting key growth initiatives, including routine capital projects, major plant expansions, and feasibility studies for new facilities. Annual capital and maintenance reinvestment at Reworld exceeds $300 million and supports long-term assets planning. While this is a corporate engineering role, it requires extensive collaboration with site/regional teams; approximately 30% of travel is expected.

Reporting to the Vice President of Engineering, this role also supports talent development, goal settings, budgeting, resource planning, feasibility studies, and project prioritizations. The Director Electrical Engineering, partners closely with cross-functional leaders, including Plant Support Engineering, Sourcing, PMO, Operations, Electrical Field Services, and Regional Engineering, to ensure discipline needs are met. The position may also support business development efforts by providing technical expertise and resourcing input.

Key Responsibilities:

Technical:

  • Discipline/Design Engineering: Manage, prioritize, and assign work across the Electrical Engineering team and SMEs.
  • Capital Projects: Lead electrical infrastructure design engineering for capital projects.
  • Technical Programs: Lead technical programs of strategic importance to the company.
  • Technical Standards: Develop, maintain, and continuously improve Reworld’s Electrical specifications/design standards library.
  • Operations Support: Provide engineering support to operations, including evaluation and implementation of technology upgrades aligned with the business needs.
  • External Engineering Partners: Engage and manage outside engineering firms to deliver technically sound, business-feasible electrical designs.
  • Front-End Loading (FEL): Lead front-end design activities for capital projects in alignment with FEL processes and tools.
  • Coaching and Mentoring: Mentor, coach, and develop SMEs, including training on FEL tools and best practices.
  • Feasibility Studies: Lead feasibility studies for new or retrofit designs, evaluating total cost of ownership (Capital and O&M) and recommending solutions that balance technical and economic considerations.

Continuous Improvement and EHS:

  • Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and Problem Solving: Lead RCAs and coach SMEs in problem-solving methodologies to implement sustainable corrective actions.
  • Lessons Learned: Drive the lessons learned program, incorporate site feedback, and update standards and specifications to improve future designs.
  • Productivity and Unscheduled Downtime: Lead improvement initiatives to reduce downtime and deliver operational savings across facilities.
  • Technical Risk Assessment: Lead technical risk assessments for electrical designs and retrofits, including SEOLDS, arc-flash studies, and protective relaying scheme reviews.
  • Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA): Lead FMEA activities to support critical troubleshooting and reliability improvements at site locations.
  • Low-Cost Country Sourcing: Perform Technical Due Diligence and provide recommendations for Projects involving Equipment sourcing from Low-cost countries.

Leadership:

  • Talent Management: Attract, develop, and retain talent; lead performance management processes for internal teams.
  • Professional Development: Provide guidance and support for talent development of Engineering SMEs.

REQUIREMENTS:

Education:

  • Bachelor of Engineering/Science (Electrical Engineering) from an accredited institution.

Experience:

  • 15–20 years of experience in an electrical engineering role, including at least five years of leadership experience.
  • Prior electrical design engineering experience in one or more of the following (or similar) industries:
    • Architectural Engineering firms
    • Data centers
    • Power generating plants
    • Large industrial facilities (Chemical, paper, co-generation or similar industries)
  • Experience with MV and HV systems (e.g., switchgear, motor control centers, protective relaying, transformers).
  • Demonstrated experience managing technical teams is required.
  • Experience across the project execution lifecycle preferred: concept design, construction, commissioning, and start-ups.
  • Experience supporting facility operations and/or maintenance is preferred.
  • Technical due diligence experience for equipment sourcing from Low-cost countries (e.g. in Asia) will be a plus.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to analyze data and identify trends.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with key stakeholders across all levels of the organization.
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects with minimal direction while providing guidance and support to a technical team of direct and indirect reports.

Certifications (preferred):

  • Professional Engineer (PE) license in the United States is highly desired.
  • Six Sigma certification (minimum Green Belt) is highly desired.

In addition to salary, this role is eligible for benefits. The benefits would include medical, prescription drug, vision, and dental plans; 401(k) plan; paid parental leave; paid time off; and paid holidays.

jobs.title: Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) & Co-founder - AI for Small Law Firms
jobs.excerpt: The OpportunityAI is changing the economics of legal practice.
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

AI is changing the economics of legal practice. Work that once took hours can increasingly be done in minutes, creating both enormous leverage for lawyers and new pressure to win and serve more clients efficiently.

Yet solo practitioners and small law firms still operate with many of the same constraints: missed calls, slow follow-up, intake handled between client matters, inconsistent marketing, and administrative work competing with billable time. Building larger intake, administrative, and marketing teams is expensive and increasingly unnecessary.

BloomLex is building a different model: a managed AI workforce that helps small law firms grow without growing their team.

The customer thesis has been validated through live pilots, and multiple deployments are moving into production evaluation. The next phase is proving in-production reliability, delivery economics, repeatability, and scalability. The companies that successfully deploy trusted AI workers into professional-service verticals over the next 18 months have an opportunity to define entirely new categories. We intend to be one of them.

The Venture

BloomLex is building an AI workforce for solo practitioners and small law firms, helping them win and serve more clients without adding headcount.

We call the broader shift the Rise of the Solo: AI gives an individual lawyer or small firm access to capabilities that historically required a much larger organization.

Unlike self-serve software, BloomLex is fully managed. We configure, deploy, monitor, and continuously improve the AI workforce for each firm. Our customers evaluate us on outcomes — calls answered, prospective clients captured, consultations booked, demand generated, follow-up completed, and time saved — not on how much software they configure themselves.

Our AI workforce starts with two teammates:

Ava — AI Front Desk. Ava answers calls 24/7, handles structured intake, screens and routes inquiries, books consultations, performs outbound callbacks and follow-up, and integrates those interactions into the firm's workflow.

Claire — AI Marketing Assistant. Claire helps firms generate and nurture demand through content, digital marketing, campaign management and optimization, lead nurturing, and ongoing marketing execution.

Together, Ava and Claire address both sides of growth: Claire helps create demand; Ava helps ensure that demand is captured and converted.

They are also the beginning, not the end, of the platform. Our roadmap expands the AI workforce across the operational side of the practice — including custom workflows and additional specialized AI roles — all delivered through the same managed model and coordinated around the lawyer.

The Partnership

The CEO co-founder is in place. The customer thesis is validated, design partners are engaged, live pilots are running, and the technology and deployment infrastructure are being built for scale.

What remains is to complete the founding team with a commercial co-founder — someone who will own revenue and go-to-market with the same conviction, urgency, and sense of ownership as the CEO and CTO.

This is not a role where you inherit a sales team, a mature playbook, and a predictable funnel. You will help discover and build those things.

You will personally close early customers, determine which channels scale, refine the commercial model from real market evidence, and then build the organization capable of repeating it.

This is a co-founder and leadership role, not simply a sales hire. You will join the CEO and CTO as one of three co-founders, with founder-level equity, founder-level responsibility, and a meaningful voice in go-to-market, pricing, hiring, fundraising, product direction, and company strategy.

What you'll own

As Co-Founder & CRO, you will own the commercial journey from first conversation through acquisition, retention, and expansion.

  • Early Revenue — Personally convert pilots and prospects into paying customers and establish the first repeatable sales motion across solo practitioners and firms of up to five lawyers.

  • Go-to-Market — Refine and operationalize our ICP, positioning, messaging, and Rise of the Solo narrative, turning them into outreach, demos, pipeline, and closed revenue.

  • Pipeline & Channels — Determine which acquisition channels actually work — outbound, content, paid acquisition, referrals, partnerships, communities, events, and others — and concentrate resources behind the ones that can scale.

  • Partnerships & Distribution — Build relationships with legal business coaches, bar associations, legal communities, consultants, complementary technology providers, and other potential distribution partners.

  • Pricing & Commercial Economics — Own pricing, packaging, expansion strategy, customer acquisition economics, retention targets, and the path toward increasing revenue per firm as the AI workforce expands.

  • Customer Success & Retention — Stay close to early customers, understand why they buy and why they stay, and build the commercial processes that turn adoption into retention, expansion, referrals, and advocacy.

  • Customer Proof — Turn early wins into measurable case studies, testimonials, references, and commercial proof around the outcomes lawyers care about.

  • Fundraising — Help tell the growth story to investors through credible traction, metrics, unit economics, forecasts, and a clear path to scale.

  • Team — Once the motion is working, recruit and lead the sales, partnerships, and customer-success organization needed to scale it.

Co-Founder Profile

We're looking for a builder first and a sales executive second.

You are likely someone who has spent enough time inside an established company to know how a professional revenue organization works — but would rather build one than inherit one.

You should bring:

  • A strong record of full-cycle selling, ideally into the legal market or another fragmented SMB/professional-services vertical.

  • The confidence to personally prospect, run demos, negotiate, close, onboard, and expand early customers before hiring people to do it for you.

  • A strong understanding of how small-business buyers make decisions, what creates trust, and how to turn an early-stage product into a compelling commercial proposition.

  • Ideally, an existing network within legal technology, solo and small-firm legal communities, bar associations, legal services, or adjacent channels.

  • Strong commercial judgment — including the willingness to challenge assumptions about positioning, pricing, channels, or markets when the evidence says we should.

  • Entrepreneurial drive: you are ready to move from selling someone else's company to building one of your own.

  • Comfort with an early-stage compensation model weighted heavily toward ownership and revenue creation rather than a conventional executive salary.

  • The ability to operate as a principal, not an employee — making decisions with the long-term value of the company in mind and doing whatever work is necessary at this stage to move it forward.

Early-stage go-to-market leadership, experience selling AI or automation products, and experience selling into the legal profession are strongly preferred. Candidates should be able to operate effectively across North American time zones.

How to Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

jobs.description:
About the Role

Retail is where COROS meets athletes in person, and across Europe it is the channel with the most room to grow and the one we are investing in now. The Retail Marketing Manager Europe turns that potential into presence, owning the marketing layer on top of our distributor and retail partner relationships across the continent. That covers digital and physical campaigns and activations, point-of-sale displays, shop windows, in-store presence and retail marketing materials, designed, sourced, produced and brought to life in five direct markets plus our distributor-led territories.

The role is also the internal interface for European leadership and sales: Country Managers and Sales Managers bring their market needs here, and this role turns them into briefs, materials and campaigns, working directly with our headquarters teams and with our US counterparts as peers. The operating principle is to build centrally and roll out locally. This role designs the European solution (concept, materials and a ready-to-use execution toolkit), and the country teams, led by the Sales Managers, run the local rollout with this role as central support. The role reports directly to the Head of Europe.

Your playground

  • Develop and execute marketing activations and campaigns with retailers and partners across Europe, in both digital and physical channels.

  • Own the marketing layer of our partner relationships: in-store presence, shop window concepts, point-of-sale displays, retail campaign mechanics and co-marketing execution.

  • Act as the single point of contact for Country Managers and Sales Managers on retail marketing needs: translate market requirements into briefs and ready-to-use toolkits, hand them to the country teams for local rollout, and keep visibility of the pipeline across all markets.

  • Brief and manage POS and display design, source and commission suppliers, manage production timelines, and coordinate distribution and stock of retail materials across European markets.

  • Localise and adapt global assets where they exist, and develop European solutions where they don't.

  • Project manage the European rollout of product launches, working between the European sales organisation and the global brand team so retail and partner execution is ready on time.

  • Design the shop staff engagement programme (product knowledge, training formats and incentive thinking) and hand it to the market teams to run with their retail partners.

  • Develop community-facing activation formats, such as community runs, where they serve retail and partner objectives.

  • Prepare and facilitate the recurring European retail review with the Head of Europe and the Country Managers, where the pipeline is prioritised across markets.

  • Work with the retail and events function in the US as a peer, and engage directly with the headquarters teams in China on asset and material requirements.

  • Track performance across retail presence and activation effectiveness, and use the data to decide where effort and spend go next.

  • Make independent spending decisions within approved projects, and bring opportunities forward proactively rather than waiting for direction.

What you bring to the starting line

Professional Background

  • Experience: 5 years+ in retail marketing, trade marketing or brand activation, ideally in sports, outdoor, consumer electronics or a comparable branded goods environment.

  • Education: Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.

  • Retail Execution: Proven track record of bringing a brand to life at the point of sale (POS concepts, in-store presence, retail campaigns) with measurable results.

  • Production and Sourcing: Hands-on experience briefing design, commissioning suppliers, managing production timelines and getting physical material where it needs to be, on time and on budget.

  • Multi-Market Work: Experience working across several time zones, cultures and markets with differing needs, and comfort as the connecting point between commercial stakeholders with varying priorities.

  • Launch Management: Experience running the marketing side of product launches across channels and markets.

Other Key Requirements

  • Collaboration and Organization: Strong project management, excellent communication, and the ability to keep many parallel workstreams moving without losing the detail.

  • Mindset: Self-motivated and resourceful. You propose rather than wait.

  • Language: Fluency in English, spoken and written. An additional European language is a plus.

  • Mobility: Willingness to travel regularly across Europe.

  • Flexibility: Willingness to occasionally work evenings or weekends around activations and events, with time off in lieu.

How the role will grow

COROS Europe is growing fast, and this role is built to grow with it. As individual markets develop enough retail volume to justify their own dedicated retail resource, the scope of this role is likely to shift: less breadth across markets, more depth in the ones that remain. How that plays out will depend on how the business develops and on the strengths the person in this role brings. This is a function being built rather than inherited, and the person building it will shape what it becomes.

The Setup

  • Reporting Line: Head of Europe.

  • Scope: Five direct European markets plus distributor-led territories.

  • Location: Remote, anywhere in the EU or the UK, ideally close to a major airport. Wherever you're based, we'll set you up with a local employment contract.

  • Working Mode: Fully remote or hybrid if you live close to an office location, with occasional team get-togethers.

  • Job Type: Full-time.

Package & Benefits

  • Work in a motivated, international team.

  • Build a function from the ground up in the channel with the most room to grow.

  • Space for ideas and independent work.

  • Flat hierarchy with short decision-making processes.

  • 25 days of paid vacation plus standard local holidays.

  • COROS products and discounts for family & friends.

  • Compensation: The base salary range for this position starts at €55.000,- annually with the possibility to earn a performance-based bonus on top. This is the least we can do for you. The final offer depends on your experience, background, and location.

jobs.description:
We are building somethingEPIC.

Evestia Clinical is a biotech-focused global CRO delivering authentic expertise and personalized support where client need it most.

Our foundation is built on four core principles: Innovation drives us to seek new solutions, Excellence defines the high standards we keep, and genuine Care ensures a supportive culture for both our patients and our people. We foster Partnership in everything we do, believing that working together—with trust and flexibility—is the key to success.

Our approach is agile by nature and personalized by design. This translates to a workplace where you are empowered to find the creative solutions necessary for our collective success. We offer a welcoming, flexible, and supportive culture that values trust and belonging, ensuring you have the support needed to grow your skills and thrive while making a difference. We partner with our clients to provide expert knowledge and guidance through complex clinical trials in rare disease, oncology, neurology, immunology, and inflammation. At Evestia Clinical, you will become a vital part of a global specialist CRO. This means you will deliver life changing impact through clinical excellence.

We are committed to creating development opportunities that allow your skills to grow right alongside ours. If you are inspired by this collaborative environment and ready to change the lives of patients worldwide, we’d love to welcome you to our team.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Pharmacovigilance Physician to provide medical leadership and expert oversight of safety data across investigational and marketed products. In this role, you will be responsible for the medical review and assessment of Individual Case Safety Reports (ICSRs), proactive signal detection and evaluation, and the review of periodic aggregate safety reports, including PBRERs and PSURs.

You will also work closely with our Medical Affairs team, providing specialist medical input and supporting the clinical medical monitoring team. This position offers the opportunity to contribute across both pharmacovigilance and broader clinical functions, helping to ensure the ongoing safety and benefit-risk assessment of the products we support.

What will your job look like?

Pharmacovigilance & Safety Operations

  • Perform robust medical review of ICSRs from clinical trials and post-marketing projects, ensuring accurate assessment of seriousness, causality, and expectedness/labeledness.

  • Review and ensure the medical accuracy and appropriateness of MedDRA and WHO Drug coding for adverse events and concomitant medications.

  • Author scientifically valid medical assessments, company comments, and concise medical summaries for complex or serious reported events.

  • Author safety-related queries to investigative sites or reporters to ensure complete and accurate clinical data collection.

  • Review and contribute to cumulative analyses of similar adverse events to support regulatory reporting and safety evaluations, including Analysis of Similar Events (AOSE) where applicable.

  • Provide medical support, guidance, mentoring, and training to the PV team, as required.

  • Review scientific literature to identify potential safety signals or valid ICSRs.

  • Apply sound medical judgment and clinical expertise to provide advice, data interpretations, and strategic guidance to PV and other internal functional departments, clients, and external partners.

  • Provide medical input for responses to regulatory authority requests, inspections, and sponsor audits and safety inquiries

Aggregate Reporting & Signal Management

  • Provide crucial medical input, review, and approval for periodic post-market and clinical safety reports, including PBRERs, PSURs, and DSURs.

  • Participate in active and routine signal detection activities. Evaluate potential safety signals, review safety data trends, and contribute to signal validation and assessment reports.

  • Contribute to integrated benefit-risk assessments throughout the product lifecycle and provide medical interpretation of evolving safety profiles.

  • Participate in or present safety data at internal Safety Management Committees (SMCs) or Data Safety Monitoring Boards (DSMBs) or sponsor safety governance meetings as contracted, providing medical interpretation, clinical context, and recommendations to support informed safety decision-making.

  • Contribute to the development and maintenance of Risk Management Plans (RMPs) and provide medical input for Safety Management Plans (SMPs).

  • Provide flexible, occasional support to the clinical medical monitoring function to ensure project continuity during peak workloads or team absences.

  • When supporting clinical operations, assist in responding to site investigators regarding protocol eligibility, safety concerns, and data management queries.

  • Perform ad-hoc medical review of clinical trial data listings, laboratory reports, and subject profiles to ensure medical accuracy and identify potential safety concerns.

Quality & Regulatory Compliance

Ensure all pharmacovigilance and medical monitoring activities comply with applicable global regulations (e.g., ICH-GVP, ICH-GCP, FDA, EMA), SOPs, and client requirements

Education:

  • Primary medical degree (e.g., MD, MBBS, MBChB, DO or equivalent) from an accredited medical school is required.

  • Active or previously held medical license/registration is required.

Experience:

  • A minimum of 2 years of experience as a physician in the pharmaceutical industry or a CRO, with a primary focus on Pharmacovigilance and Drug Safety.

  • Proven, hands-on experience performing medical review of ICSRs.

  • Experience with aggregate safety report (PBRERs, PSURs, DSURs) review and generation is a plus.

  • Working knowledge of global regulations regarding drug safety and pharmacovigilance (ICH, FDA, EMA).

  • Strong scientific, clinical, and analytical knowledge with excellent ability to read, analyze, and interpret scientific data.

  • Demonstrated ability to analyze and interpret complex scientific and clinical data.

Competencies & Skills

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills, with the ability to interact effectively with Investigators, clients, and regulatory authorities.

  • Highly proficient in utilizing electronic applications, specifically the ability to efficiently navigate clinical and pharmacovigilance safety databases to conduct medical reviews and extract data.

  • Ability to exercise independent medical judgment and make timely, evidence-based decisions in time-sensitive situations, including complex safety assessments, benefit-risk evaluation, signal management, and clinical trial eligibility support when required.

  • Excellent cross-functional collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary teams and with external stakeholders.

  • Strong knowledge of MedDRA and WHO Drug coding dictionaries.

What we offer you in return?

We believe that to do your best work, you need the best support. That's why we care deeply about your wellbeing, personal development, and achieving a true work-life balance.

As part of our team, you'll have the opportunity to influence patient safety on a global scale while working with talented colleagues who share a passion for scientific excellence. We offer a collaborative and flexible working environment, opportunities for professional growth, and the chance to contribute to meaningful work that ultimately benefits patients around the world.

Ready to Take the Next Step?

Does joining Evestia Clinical and making a global impact excite you? Then it's time to apply!

We are eager to meet ambitious candidates. Remember, we hire for potential and passion. Therefore if you feel you're a good fit but don't meet every single requirement, please submit your application anyway. We want to hear from you.

Develop and manage lending relationships for the purpose of generating loan requests that meet established lending requirements, which provide maximum profitability to the bank with a minimum risk. Including managing a loan portfolio for the express purpose of increasing balances and profit, and decreasing past dues, charge-offs, and other loan problems.   • Develop an on-going personal business development plan that utilizes a structured calling program that generates an agreed-to minimum of new loan growth and fee generation based on business unit KPIs.

  • Promote bank services, seek out referral opportunities (including consumer loans), answer customer questions, and direct customers to the appropriate personnel for assistance.

  • Maintain a working knowledge of all legal and regulatory compliance issues as they pertain to this position.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Ability to sit for extended periods of time, twist, bend, sit, walk use hands to twist, handle or feel objects, tools or controls, such as computer mouse, computer keyboard, calculator, stapler, telephone, staple puller, etc., reach with hands and arms, balance, stoop, kneel, talk or hear.
  • Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and the ability to adjust focus.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree from a four-year college or university preferred but will consider experience in lieu of degree.
  • Proven track record in commercial lending, specifically for commercial and commercial real estate loan requests.
  • Relationship management skills for commercial, small business, and personal relationships.
  • Highly developed analytical and underwriting expertise and a credit quality focus.
  • Portfolio management experience required.
  • Strong oral and written communication skills.
  • Proficient computer skills.
  • Excellent customer service skills.

THE COMPANY

Founded in 1912, Stearns Financial Services Inc. (SFSI) is a $3.2 billion, independently owned financial institution with locations in Minnesota, Florida and Arizona, and over 35,000 small business customers nationwide. Specializing in affordable housing financing, USDA and SBA lending, and small business and equipment financing, Stearns Bank is regularly recognized as one of the country’s top-performing banks and “Best Banks to Work For” by American Banker.

jobs.excerpt: ESQlabs is an innovative, internationally active Contract Research Organization (CRO) and a global leader in the development and application of the Open Systems Pharmacology (OSP) Suite.
jobs.description:
ESQlabs is an innovative, internationally active Contract Research Organization (CRO) and a global leader in the development and application of the Open Systems Pharmacology (OSP) Suite. We combine mechanistic modeling, Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetics (PBPK) and Quantitative Systems Pharmacology (QSP), with software and training to support Model-Informed Drug Development (MIDD) and Next-Generation Risk Assessment (NGRA) for pharmaceutical, chemical, and academic partners worldwide. Our mission is to empower life sciences: helping scientists understand mechanisms of disease and chemical toxicity to optimize individualized, safer, and more efficient treatment and testing strategies.

We are building a platform where AI agents help scientists set up regulated modeling analyses, and fixed, versioned procedures run them. This job is about the engine room: the compute core, the release pipeline and the operations.

About the role

You make sure our analyses can be reproduced, shipped to clients and checked later. You own the compute core, the release pipeline, deployment into client environments, and the metering and provenance behind every result. The AI layer has its own lead and team; you build what they run on. The Quality Manager sets the standards, you implement them. You report to the CEO.

Key Responsibilities

  • Make the scientific compute core deterministic: pinned R, Python and solver toolchains, content-addressed container images with a software bill of materials, and tests that prove byte-identical re-execution on a reference platform and tolerance-bounded re-execution across platforms.

  • Build the services the AI layer runs on: isolated executors per client without network access, usage metering per call, the signed record and the certificate behind every result. You build the policy engine and the tool router together with the AI lead.

  • Expose the platform as a versioned API and as tools for AI agents with one shared contract, and ship the reproducibility package that re-executes a run outside the platform.

  • Run the evaluation pipeline in continuous integration: conformance tests against reference case sets, re-execution tests, regression tests, results stored per procedure version.

  • Own release engineering and operations: CI/CD pipelines, signed and content-addressed releases, scripted installation qualification, environment management (hosted, in a client tenant, later offline), monitoring, incident handling and the operating model the deployment engineer runs.

  • Implement the technical controls behind the information security and AI management standards the Quality Manager owns.


What you bring

  • At least five years of platform, infrastructure or backend engineering with senior ownership of a production system.

  • Reproducible builds and execution in practice: dependency pinning, artifact hashing, immutable versioning, supply chain integrity. Hermetic build systems are a strong plus.

  • Kubernetes or a similar orchestrator, monitoring, and release management for environments you don’t fully control.

  • API design where the schema was a contract with external consumers, including versioning and deprecation in practice.

  • Security engineering for multi-tenant systems: isolation, secrets, authorization, and awareness of the risks of language-model-driven systems. Exposure to GxP or equivalent regulated software is valuable; interest in acquiring it is required.

What's in store for you

The dynamic team behind ESQlabs unites people with different backgrounds, spanning disciplines like pharmaceutical sciences, physics, bioinformatics, mathematics, data science, and software engineering. Our trust in each other, our open-mindedness, and our constant quest for excellence and innovation unite us. We value flat hierarchies, where everyone can contribute ideas and expertise to develop the best product. We are passionate, always willing to broaden our horizons, and love our start-up culture.

You will also benefit from:

  • Flexible work hours and a home office policy that focuses on people and not on numbers

  • An attractive remuneration package

  • Regular in-person team gatherings at locations across Europe.

  • A clearly defined technical problem with a commercial consequence, and the authority to solve it properly rather than quickly.

  • A working environment in which your contribution will make a difference, and that allows you to take ownership of projects and processes

  • A small, senior team that owns an open-source platform used by regulators and pharma, and the mandate to set the standard for certified scientific software.

  • Responsibility, autonomy, participation, and career perspective

About us

We collaborate with global corporations in the pharma and chemical industry, as well as start-ups in the life-science technology sector and academic and non-profit research institutions. We define new standards in pharmacometrics and systems pharmacology and toxicology areas. Our software and model platforms help scientists understand mechanisms of diseases and chemical toxicity to optimize individualized treatment of patients and protect the health of the animal and human life.

ESQlabs has attracted international players as sponsors for the OSP Software development. In addition, funding through national and EU-wide research grants allows us to develop our core technologies continuously.

For more information about our culture, values and benefits visit our Unique career opportunities - esqLABS GmbH.

ESQlabs is an equal-opportunity employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of background, and value the diversity of perspectives this brings to our team.

The individual will be responsible for translating study protocols, statistical analysis plans (SAPs), and analysis specifications into high-quality, reproducible programming solutions and study outputs.

The Real-World Analytics Programmer will partner closely with HEOR/RWE scientists, data scientists, biostatisticians, and other cross-functional stakeholders to support the successful execution of observational research studies. The role requires strong technical expertise, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple studies and competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.

  • Works with multiple oncology-focused real-world data assets, including claims, electronic health records (EHR), genomic testing databases, and linked clinical-genomic datasets.

  • Assesses data quality, completeness, and fitness-for-purpose and provide recommendations regarding data availability and implementation feasibility.

  • Independently performs quality control and validation activities for programming code, analysis datasets, and study outputs.

  • Develops and maintains technical documentation, programming specifications, reusable code, macros, and reproducible analytic workflows for assigned studies.

  • Stays current with evolving industry best practices, technologies, and regulatory expectations related to oncology real-world data and evidence generation.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

  • BS/MS degree in Statistics, Biostatistics, Computer Science, Data Science, Epidemiology, Mathematics, or a related quantitative discipline.

  • 8+ years of statistical programming experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, CRO, healthcare research, or related settings for Senior-level candidates.

  • Demonstrated experience independently leading programming activities for observational research, HEOR, epidemiology, or real-world evidence studies.

  • Strong SAS or R programming experience required, including experience developing analysis datasets and study deliverables from complex healthcare data sources.

  • Experience with SQL required and working knowledge of R or other programming language for data manipulation, analytics support, and quality control activities preferred.

  • Experience developing analysis datasets, tables, listings, and figures (TLFs) from complex healthcare or real-world data sources.

  • Experience working with large healthcare databases, including claims, EHR, genomic, registry, or linked clinical-genomic datasets.

  • Strong understanding of observational research workflows and implementation of study specifications.

  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously while meeting timelines and quality expectations.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail.

  • Thrives in a collaborative team environment and is motivated to drive high-quality technical execution and continuous process improvement.

Preferred Skills:

  • Experience working with major oncology or healthcare real-world data assets, such as Flatiron Health, ConcertAI, COTA, Tempus, Guardant, Merative MarketScan, Komodo, Optum, TriNetX, or similar datasets.

  • Experience supporting HTA, market access, indirect treatment comparison (ITC), external control arm, or regulatory-grade real-world evidence studies.

  • Experience developing reusable programming frameworks, standardized macros, and validation tools.

Entry-Level Freight Dispatcher — Remote

Turn your communication, organization, and problem-solving skills into a career in U.S. trucking and logistics.

Truck Driver Nation LLC is hiring a full-time Entry-Level Freight Dispatcher to work directly with our team and support our U.S. freight-dispatch operations from a remote, work-from-home environment.

Previous freight-dispatch experience is preferred but not required. Candidates with transferable experience in trucking, transportation, logistics, customer service, sales, operations, scheduling, coordination, or other fast-paced professional environments are encouraged to apply.

Direct freight-dispatch experience is not required for every candidate. Relevant professional experience, transferable skills, transportation knowledge, and the ability to learn quickly will also be considered.

What You'll Do

As an Entry-Level Freight Dispatcher, you will help coordinate freight movement and maintain communication between drivers and the businesses involved in moving each load.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Search and evaluate available freight based on truck location, equipment, mileage, rates, and operational requirements.
  • Communicate professionally with drivers, brokers, carriers, shippers, receivers, and customers.
  • Negotiate freight rates when authorized.
  • Calculate mileage and rate per mile when evaluating potential loads.
  • Plan loads and assist with efficient trip planning.
  • Coordinate pickup and delivery appointments and requirements.
  • Monitor active loads from pickup through delivery.
  • Maintain accurate dispatch records, load notes, and documentation.
  • Provide timely status updates and follow up on active shipments.
  • Assist drivers with routine issues that arise during dispatched loads.
  • Identify delays, scheduling conflicts, or other operational issues and communicate them promptly.
  • Maintain professional working relationships with drivers, brokers, carriers, and customers.

What We're Looking For

  • Freight-dispatch experience is preferred but not required.
  • Relevant experience in trucking, transportation, logistics, customer service, sales, scheduling, operations, administrative coordination, or similar professional environments will be considered.
  • Fluent spoken and written English.
  • Strong professional communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving abilities.
  • Confidence communicating by phone, email, and web-based business systems.
  • Ability to perform basic mileage and rate-per-mile calculations accurately.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining attention to detail.
  • Ability to work independently and remain accountable in a remote environment.
  • Computer suitable for daily professional remote work.
  • Reliable high-speed internet connection.
  • Reliable and professional work-from-home environment.
  • Availability during required U.S. freight-operating hours.
  • Familiarity with U.S. trucking, transportation, or logistics operations is an advantage.

Who May Do Well in This Role

You may be a strong candidate if you naturally think ahead, communicate confidently, pay attention to details, and understand how individual decisions can affect a driver's time, a customer's freight, and the profitability of a truck.

Direct freight-dispatch experience can be valuable, but it is not the only relevant background. Strong communication, customer service, sales, transportation knowledge, scheduling experience, problem-solving ability, and experience coordinating multiple moving parts can transfer well into this position.

Schedule

Full-time, Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Central Time. Schedule adjustments may occasionally be required based on active freight operations, pickup and delivery requirements, or driver needs.

Compensation

$20.00–$25.00 per hour, based on experience and qualifications.

Ready for Your Next Move?

If you have strong communication skills, attention to detail, sound judgment, and the ability to stay organized in a fast-moving transportation environment, submit your application to Truck Driver Nation LLC for consideration for this Entry-Level Freight Dispatcher position.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight! 

Blue Origin is pioneering the future of space-based connectivity with TeraWave, a revolutionary satellite communications network designed to deliver symmetrical data speeds of up to 6 Tbps anywhere on Earth. This network will service tens of thousands of enterprise, data center, and government users who require reliable connectivity for critical operations.

Job Description

Blue Origin is seeking a Principal ASIC Test Engineer to lead production test strategy for RF, mmWave, and mixed-signal integrated circuits within Silicon Systems.

This individual contributor role serves as the technical lead for final test of mmWave front-end ICs and converter-intensive ASICs, with focus on RF/mmWave performance, high-speed ADC and DAC testing, manufacturability, and cost of test.

The role leads test engagement with manufacturing and OSAT partners and mentors internal test engineers supporting front-end IC and digital beamformer programs.

Special Mentions

- Relocation provided

- Travel expected up to 15% of the time

- Interviews will include a technical assessment

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Define wafer sort and final test strategies, coverage targets, and production release criteria for RF and mixed-signal devices.
  • Develop and optimize ATE tests for RF signal chains, frequency conversion, PLLs, clocking, and high-speed ADCs and DACs.
  • Establish test approaches for packaged RF devices, including antenna-in-package calibration, fixture design, and correlation to laboratory measurements.
  • Partner with design and DFT teams to improve test access, observability, and production test efficiency during development.
  • Lead technical work with foundry, manufacturing, and OSAT partners on probe and final test implementation, throughput, and failure analysis.
  • Mentor test engineers and provide test domain guidance across front-end IC and digital beamformer programs.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or related field and 10 years of semiconductor test experience.
  • Experience developing wafer sort and final test programs on production ATE platforms, including Advantest V93000.
  • Demonstrated experience with RF or mmWave testing and high-speed ADC and DAC testing.
  • Experience taking test programs from silicon bring-up through manufacturing release with external partners.

jobs.description:
The Opportunity

FutureSight is seeking a Co-Founder & CEO to leadLoomwork, an AI automation venture. This is a co-founder partnership with meaningful founder equity, not a salaried executive role.

Loomworkis an AI automation agency for growing companies. Every growing company knows AI is its next growth lever, but few have the people to turn it into working systems. Implementation is the scarce resource.Loomworkhelps them find where AI will pay off, builds agents into the tools they already use, and keeps those agents running. It launches as a services business with a dedicated technical delivery team from day one. Every engagement also serves as research: as client work converges on one segment, Loomwork turns its library of deployed agents into a connected product and grows from agency to software company.

Market Context

The global AI consulting services market is valued at $11.9B in 2026 and is projected to reach $73.9B by 2034, growing at a 25.6% CAGR. North America holds about 38% of the market. Enterprise AI adoption climbed from 20% in 2017 to 88% in 2025, and adoption is outpacing the talent available to deploy it. Roughly 190,000 US and Canadian companies fall in the $10M to $300M revenue range, which puts the serviceable market at an estimated $3B a year. Most of these companies are too large for freelancers and too small for enterprise firms.

About FutureSight

FutureSight is a leading venture builder that co-creates world-class software companies with values-driven entrepreneurs from inception to exit. We are a team of founders, operators and designers with experience successfully bringing software to market at scale.

You’ll co-create with a proven venture building team, led by John Carbrey (4x entrepreneur, $100M ARR), Krista LaRiviere (3x exited, E&Y Top Women Entrepreneur), Alan Smith (Strategyzer co-founder, $120M in products built), Prathna Ramesh (former MD of Maple Leaf Angels, $275M in follow-on capital), and Johnny Tong (0-to-1 builder, acquired by SAP and Stripe) bring a rare combination of operator exits, institutional investing, and AI product depth.

The Partnership

  • Founder equity with meaningful ownership from inception

  • Pre-seed capital committed by FutureSight for early hires and MVP development, with potential for follow-on funding

  • Venture building resources, including embedded design, engineering, growth, and fundraising support from day one

  • Investor and advisor network across the industry and early-stage capital markets

  • A true co-creation model in which you operate as CEO with FutureSight’s cross-functional team as your partner

What You’ll Own

As Co-Founder & CEO, you will set the direction of the venture and lead its execution.

  • Strategy: Shape the service offering, pricing, and positioning, and choose the segment to specialize in based on where demand converges

  • Customer Development: Win engagements with growing companies, move clients from assessment to build to retainer, and build the go-to-market motion

  • Product: Partner with the FutureSight delivery and engineering team to turn repeated client builds into reusable agents and, ultimately, a connected product

  • Capital: Lead future fundraising, supported by FutureSight's network and the agency's traction

  • Team: Recruit and lead the founding team, including a technical leader as the product takes shape, and establish the cultural foundation of the company

Co-Founder Profile

  • Previous founding experience at a venture-backed company

  • Demonstrated success in B2B SaaS go-to-market, including sales and customer engagement

  • Fundraising fluency, with the ability to develop investor narratives and close capital

  • Proven ability to attract, develop, and retain top talent

  • Clear-eyed understanding of the risks and demands of co-founding a venture-backed company

  • Direct exposure to AI implementation, consulting, or selling technology services into growing companies

How to Apply

Please submit your resume, LinkedIn profile, and a brief note on why this venture aligns with your goals as a founder. We will move quickly for the right candidate.

FutureSight is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and experiences.

If that sounds like a fun problem rather than a scary one, keep reading.

This is a co-founder role, not a CTO hire. In return for that level of commitment, you receive founder-level equity, founder-level authority with co-decision rights on product, technology, hiring, fundraising, and strategy, and a genuine partnership with the CEO on every material decision.

THE COMPANY
Established in early 2024, at Analogue Insight we are bridging the Analogue and Digital Worlds for Tomorrow through our Chiplet Solutions.
